item.title: Is Progress Possible Without People? Navigating Quality of Life Between Homo Sapiens and Homo Digitalis
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the tension between human wellbeing and technological advancement in contemporary society. It investigates how progress can be defined and achieved when considering the interplay between traditional human values and the emerging digital dimension of human existence, asking whether societal advancement necessarily requires prioritizing technological development over human quality of life.

The issue invites contributions that explore socio-economic dimensions of human-digital coexistence, considering how societies can navigate the balance between innovation and maintaining or enhancing quality of life for human populations.

Appel publié par Socio-Economic Planning Sciences. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Quality of life
  • Human-digital relationships
  • Progress and development
  • Socio-economic impacts
  • Digital transformation

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) for Tariffs and Supply Chains: Pathways to Resilient Economic Planning
item.content:encoded:
This special issue focuses on applying multi-criteria decision analysis methodologies to address challenges related to tariffs and supply chain management. The collection seeks research that demonstrates how MCDA frameworks can inform more resilient approaches to economic planning in increasingly complex and interconnected global markets.

item.title: Operations Research and Data-Driven Decision Making for Complex Socio-Economic Systems in Ibero-America: Evidence and Applications
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks research that applies operations research and data-driven methodologies to address complex socio-economic challenges within Ibero-American countries. The focus is on demonstrating how quantitative and analytical approaches can inform policy decisions and solve real-world problems affecting social and economic systems in this region.

item.title: Technology-enhanced learning in developing countries: the impact on entrepreneurial education and innovation
item.content:encoded:
